newsitem.title: USA: Sun refinery project, lower margins hurt Q4.
newsitem.headline: Sun refinery project, lower margins hurt Q4.

text.p: Sun Co Inc said a $41 million decline in its fourth quarter operating results was largely attributable to significantly lower gasoline margins and the absence of earnings from its Sun International Production business, which was sold in September 1996.

The company said a scheduled refinery maintenance turnaround at its Marcus Hook Refinery in Pennsylvania also depressed its results. The Marcus Hook maintenance turnaround was the largest in Sun's history.
Sun posted an operating loss of $23 million in the quarter, compared to an $18 million profit a year earlier.

The latest quarterly results excluded $201 million in after-tax charges. Among those was an $85 million after-tax writedown for estimated losses through May 2000 for the company's off-take agreement to purchase MTBE from Belvieu Environmental Fuels.

The agreement requires Sun to purchase all the MBTE production from a 14,000 barrel-per-day facility at contract prices that currently exceed market prices. Belvieu Environmental Fuels, located in Mont Belvieu, Texas, is partially owned by Sun.
Sun expects the adverse price relationship will continue through May 2000, after which the contract reflects existing market conditions.
MBTE is an oxygenate used in making reformulated gasoline as mandated by the Clean Air Act of 1990.
